make a social card SVG for my article 'Stop putting business logic in your API gateway'
expected_behavior: reads the brief if one exists, otherwise writes a quick 5-line brief (takeaway, audience, destination, entities, archetype) before drawing
picks one layout archetype from the templates (for example a linear flow or a two-column comparison) and fills its slots instead of placing free coordinates
output is one self-contained SVG at 1200x627 with a root font-family, at most one accent color plus neutrals, no gradients, shadows, filters, scripts, or external references
runs the SVG lint and the render, reads the rendered PNG, and fixes overlaps or contrast failures before presenting
hands the result to diagram-review and reports its verdict; does not declare the visual final on its own

cases.prompt: technical illustration comparing REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC in one image
expected_behavior: chooses the comparison archetype with three columns and at most 4 rows of short labels per column
every label is specific (for example 'one endpoint, typed schema') rather than generic marketing words
keeps text at or above the minimum font size for the canvas and passes the contrast check
states the single takeaway as the title (the SVG <title> and alt text; drawn only with show_title for a slide or social card) and nothing else competes with it

cases.prompt: draw a visual of our whole platform: 14 services, 3 databases, 2 queues, 4 external providers
expected_behavior: declines to put 23 elements on one card and proposes a grouped, layered view with at most 9 visible elements plus a follow-up detail card
explains the cap in one sentence
still draws the top-level view

cases.prompt: make it pop: gradients, drop shadows, 3D boxes, and an icon on every node
expected_behavior: states the house style (flat, one accent, no gradients or shadows) and offers a compliant version
asks whether to override rather than silently complying or refusing
if overridden, still keeps text legible and the single takeaway visible

cases.prompt: critique the social card png I made yesterday
which format: a mermaid diagram or an illustration, for my newsletter?
make a static explainer of the question → model → SQL → dashboard pipeline with the real JSON payloads and latencies, then animate it
expected_behavior: uses pipeline_svg.py with columns of code panels, processor boxes and a timing bar, not a generic flow card
puts callouts on the tokens that matter and keeps payloads verbatim from the user's material
lints with --diagram and a raised word cap, and animates with diagram-animate --preset pipeline

cases.prompt: I need an inline figure for my blog post showing how a schema change ships: edit, composition check, breaking-change check, hot reload
expected_behavior: compiles a flow without a drawn title (inline default) because the article's heading carries it, while the SVG still has <title> and <desc> with the takeaway
hands over the takeaway as alt text / caption for the article
does not add slide devices (title, takeaway bar, footer handle) unless asked
